title: The Lasker Trap
subtitle: An underpromotion on move seven wins a queen (Albin).
goals: Punish greedy pawn grabs in the Albin
Recognize the trap from both sides

steps.say: The Albin Countergambit: 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e5!? — Black offers a pawn for a monster on d4. White just played 4.e3?, trying to dissolve that pawn, and stepped into the Lasker Trap: a forced sequence featuring the rarest beauty in chess — a knight UNDERPROMOTION on move seven that wins the queen. You're Black. Nine moves of mayhem start with a bishop check.

steps.prompt: White's 4.e3? was the losing move. Play the whole punishment — bishop check, pawn storm, and the famous underpromotion!
hints: Start with Bb4+ — the block on d2 is forced-ish, and then your d-pawn starts eating: dxe3, exf2+, and the promotion square g1 has a surprise on it.
When your pawn reaches g1, do NOT take a queen — Rxg1 would follow with check-safety. Promote to a KNIGHT with check, and the g4-bishop check wins the queen next.

line.say: Check! White must block — and the natural Bd2 walks deeper into the pit.
The pawn bites — threatening the bishop on d2 AND f2. White grabs your bishop, believing he's winning a piece...
...but the pawn storms on with check. The king must step out (Kxf2?? drops the king into ...Qh4+ ideas; Ke2 is the main line)...
THE MOVE. A knight, not a queen! Underpromotion WITH CHECK — a new queen would allow Rxg1 with the king safe, but the knight check forces the rook to capture with the king still stranded on e2...
The point: check on g4, and whatever blocks or moves, the d1 queen falls next. Emanuel Lasker's namesake trap — a whole queen won by refusing one.

rejections.say: Development at the wrong second — White plays exd4 and breathes again, a healthy pawn up. The window is NOW, while e3 hangs in the air: Bb4+!
One move early! After fxe3 the storm fizzles — White's king keeps f2 covered. The bishop check comes FIRST: Bb4+ forces the block that clogs White's escape.

steps.wrongSay: The sequence is forced from the first check: Bb4+, then let the d-pawn feed.
steps.successSay: fxg1=N+!! — one of the only famous underpromotions in opening theory, and you played the whole nine-move trap.

steps.say: The other side of the coin: if you face the Albin as White, the losing move was 4.e3?. The safe path: develop normally with 4.Nf3 and 5.g3 — let the d4 pawn sit, don't try to dissolve it. Traps punish greed and haste; knowing WHERE the mine is buried means you'll never step on it.
